tldr: We propose $\lambda_{0}$, a humanoid foundation model that drastically boosts real-world loco-manipulation performance. It uses 500 hours of whole-body human motion data collected purely via wearable devices without physical robots, aligned for humanoids and trained across three stages.
hero_caption: An overview diagram of the study. It illustrates wearable-based egocentric whole-body human data collection (HumanVerse), human-to-humanoid observation and action alignment, the three-stage training pipeline (pre-training, mid-training, real-robot post-training), and significant performance gains on the physical Unitree G1 humanoid.
overview:
Whole-body loco-manipulation with bipedal humanoids is an extremely challenging task requiring whole-body coordination. Achieving this via imitation learning typically demands scaling whole-body teleoperation directly on physical robots. However, operating physical robots is laborious, costly, and hard to scale across diverse real-world environments.

To address this, the authors asked: can we collect massive amounts of everyday human activities using only wearable sensors, without any physical robots? While prior methods utilized egocentric hand trajectories, they often omitted locomotion and posture changes. Moreover, embodiment discrepancies and controller tracking dynamics caused end-effector errors, frequently failing contact-rich tasks. To bridge this gap, the team built HumanVerse, a 500-hour egocentric dataset spanning 827 diverse daily tasks with synchronized body and hand motion. They also developed a Human-to-Humanoid Alignment pipeline that progressively corrects morphology gaps and controller tracking offline.

Using this aligned human data, the team trained $\lambda_{0}$, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation model. The training follows three stages: hand-centric pre-training, whole-body human mid-training with HumanVerse, and real-robot post-training with a small amount of teleoperation data. Real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid demonstrated that $\lambda_{0}$ significantly outperformed robot-only training and leading baselines like StarVLA and GR00T. This milestone shows that scaling whole-body human motion data directly translates into scalable physical action capabilities for humanoids.
contributions: Developed an alignment pipeline that automatically converts and corrects human whole-body motion data collected without robots across appearance, kinematics, and dynamics for humanoids (Unitree G1).
Built HumanVerse, a 500-hour open-world dataset pairing egocentric video with fully synchronized whole-body and hand motions across daily environments.
Proposed $\lambda_{0}$, a whole-body loco-manipulation VLA model trained via a three-stage pipeline: egocentric hand pre-training, whole-body human mid-training, and real-robot adaptation.
Experimentally proved that scaling whole-body human data consistently lowers validation loss and monotonically improves downstream task progress on physical hardware.

sections.heading: Breaking the Teleoperation Bottleneck: Can Egocentric Human Data Fuel Humanoids?
sections.summary: Humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation demands massive data, but real-robot teleoperation is prohibitively expensive. This paper introduces an offline pipeline to accurately retarget wearable-captured human actions to humanoids, along with the foundation model $\lambda_{0}$.
sections.details:
Teaching humanoids complex tasks requires coordinated data of walking, squatting, and manipulation. Mainstream full-body teleoperation on physical robots places a heavy burden on operators. Hardware constraints also bottleneck data collection across diverse environments.

In contrast, human motion data captured with egocentric cameras like GoPro is easy to collect at scale. However, existing video-based methods track only hand or wrist trajectories, missing locomotion and posture shifts like bending down. Furthermore, directly streaming human motions to a robot causes end-effector offsets of several to tens of centimeters due to kinematic differences and controller tracking delays, resulting in failed grasping and contact.

Therefore, the authors tackled a key question: Can we generate high-precision, robot-executable demonstration data offline entirely from egocentric human data? By combining visual synthesis with a three-stage motion alignment, they achieved strong zero-shot transfer without any target-task robot demonstrations.

sections.heading: From Human Video Imitation to Humanoid Whole-Body Control
sections.summary: The paper reviews generalist robot models, learning from human video, and humanoid whole-body control, highlighting its unique position in exploring uncharted territory: scaling synchronized whole-body data.
sections.details:
Related work falls into three main areas.

### Advances in Generalist Robot Policies
Generalist robot policies that aggregate diverse robot data, such as Open X-Embodiment and $\pi_0$, are advancing rapidly. Portable data collection tools like UMI have also emerged. However, these primarily target tabletop arms or quadrupeds and do not cover the vast action space of bipedal humanoids.

### Robot Learning from Human Videos
Many methods reconstruct hand trajectories from large-scale video datasets like Ego4D for manipulation pre-training. Yet most focus on static tabletop setups. While recent works like EMMA address whole-body motion, systematic data scaling for bipedal whole-body coordination remained unexplored.

### Humanoid Whole-Body Control and Retargeting
Techniques for retargeting human motion to humanoids (such as GMR and Human2Humanoid) and RL-based tracking controllers (like SONIC) have been developed. This paper's approach stands out by going beyond geometric retargeting: it incorporates offline optimization accounting for controller tracking dynamics and directly couples it into a VLA training pipeline.

sections.heading: 500 Hours Without Robots: HumanVerse Collection and Embodiment Alignment
sections.summary: Introduces HumanVerse, a 500-hour whole-body dataset gathered across diverse everyday locations. The key is a sophisticated pipeline that bridges embodiment gaps and slashes tracking errors down to centimeter-level accuracy.
sections.details:
### 3.1 Data Collection Setup and Protocol
Data collectors wear a neck-mounted GoPro HERO13 (aligned with the robot's head camera height and field of view) alongside a PICO 4 Ultra VR headset and five trackers. Without physical robots on-site, collection spans homes, supermarkets, offices, and outdoor environments. Collectors receive task-level instructions rather than rigid joint trajectories. This naturally includes walking approaches, posture shifts, and regrasp maneuvers.

### 3.2 Dataset Scale and Diversity
HumanVerse totals 500 hours across 32,993 episodes and about 87 million frames. It spans 827 task types, including cleaning, cooking, laundry, and parcel transport. It is rich in coordinated motions like crouching to reach low objects or carrying large boxes with both hands while walking.

### 3.3 Motion Reconstruction and Annotation
By cross-correlating GoPro gyroscope data and PICO tracker angular velocity, timestamps across both unsynchronized clocks align with millisecond precision. Kinematics for 24 body joints come from trackers, while 21 joints per hand are accurately reconstructed from RGB video using Dyn-HaMR.

### 3.4 Human-to-Humanoid Alignment
Feeding raw human motions directly to the G1 causes execution failure, so two alignment steps are applied:
- **Observation Alignment**: Human arms and trackers are segmented via SAM2 and inpainted using DiffuEraser. Rendered G1 robot arms are then composited on top, matching the robot's own visual perspective.
- **Action Alignment**: End-effector discrepancies under the tracking controller (SONIC) are corrected in three stages. First, body morphology differences are rescaled (human reference). Second, whole-body inverse kinematics (IK) adjusts for robot link lengths (robot reference). Finally, latent tokens are directly optimized via gradients using dynamics simulation rollout feedback (dynamics optimization). This reduces end-effector position error from 17.03 cm to 3.83 cm and orientation error from 36.06° to 10.85°.

sections.heading: Three-Stage Training: From Hand Actions to Whole-Body Coordination and Real Hardware
sections.summary: Explains the model architecture and three-stage training strategy of the VLA foundation model $\lambda_{0}$. Progressive learning from egocentric hand data to whole-body HumanVerse mid-training and real-robot post-training unlocks efficient physical control.
sections.details:
### 4.1 Architecture and Action Representation
$\lambda_{0}$ connects a Qwen3.5-2B vision-language backbone with a generative Action Expert. The 44-dimensional robot state input (29 body joints, 12 hand joints, 3 gravity vector components) is tokenized into discrete tokens and concatenated after language instructions. The model outputs a 50-step action chunk. Each step comprises a 64-dimensional motion latent for the SONIC controller and 12-dimensional control commands for the Revo2 hands (76 dimensions total).

### 4.2 Three-Stage Training Pipeline
Training proceeds through three stages:
- **Stage I (Egocentric Hand Pre-training)**: Pre-trains on seven public egocentric hand datasets to predict future bimanual state tokens (discretized hand poses and joints). The Action Expert is not used here; only the vision-language backbone is trained.
- **Stage II (Whole-body Human Mid-training)**: Introduces the Action Expert and trains whole-body coordination on aligned HumanVerse data. A domain embedding absorbs differences between human and robot data.
- **Stage III (Real-robot Post-training)**: Adapts the policy to target robot (Unitree G1) dynamics using a small amount of physical teleoperation data.

### 4.3 Loss Function and Deployment
Stages II and III employ a Flow Matching velocity field prediction loss. During inference, actions are generated from noise via a 10-step Euler integration. At real-world deployment, no human sensors are needed; G1 operates autonomously using only its onboard head camera and joint feedback.

sections.heading: Proving the Power of Scale: Reaching a 62.5% Success Rate on Real Robots
sections.summary: Evaluated in simulation (SIMPLE) and on physical Unitree G1 humanoids. $\lambda_{0}$ substantially outperformed strong baselines, confirming that scaling human data monotonically improves real-world task progress.
sections.details:
### 5.1 Efficiency and Impact of Aligned Human Data
Even under zero-shot conditions without target-task robot data, policies trained purely on action-aligned human data achieved an average progress of 51.7% on whole-body manipulation and 76.2% on long-range loco-manipulation. In terms of collection efficiency, human data collection achieved roughly 76.4% effort reduction per episode (~4.2x throughput) compared to real-robot teleoperation.

### 5.2 Real-Robot and Simulation Task Performance
Evaluations on physical G1 covered four demanding loco-manipulation tasks: toy packing, dual-arm bin transport, bottle disposal into a pedal trashcan, and chair pushing under a desk.
- **Real-Robot Results**: $\lambda_{0}$ achieved a 62.5% success rate and 80.4% weighted progress. This vastly outperformed StarVLA (40.0% success, 54.6% progress) and GR00T N1.6 (7.5% success). On the bottle disposal task requiring coordinated foot stomping, it achieved 80.0% progress.
- **Simulation Results**: On the SIMPLE benchmark, $\lambda_{0}$ reached a 90.0% overall success rate, outperforming baselines like StarVLA (86.1%).

### 5.3 Scaling Laws and Ablations
Varying Stage II (HumanVerse) data scale across 0%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100% revealed a steady drop in validation loss and a monotonic rise in real-robot task progress from 59.9% to 80.4%.
Ablations showed that removing Stage II (whole-body mid-training) caused real-world success to plummet from 62.5% down to 22.5%. Whole-body mid-training proved to be far more decisive for loco-manipulation success than hand-only pre-training (Stage I).

### 5.4 Generalization to Unseen Objects
The team tested generalization on objects present during human data collection but unseen during robot post-training (Instance B). $\lambda_{0}$ improved average progress from 48.4% to 55.8% compared to a robot-only baseline, confirming that human data aids visual and manipulation generalization.

sections.heading: Conclusion: Whole-Body Human Data Ushers in a New Era for Humanoid Foundation Models
sections.summary: Proposed the humanoid foundation model $\lambda_{0}$ and the 500-hour dataset HumanVerse. Concludes that large-scale human data collection without robots, paired with proper alignment, is a highly viable path toward scaling embodied intelligence.
sections.details:
This work demonstrates that egocentric whole-body human data collected without physical robots serves as a potent learning resource for humanoid loco-manipulation.

Rather than leaping directly from hand video pre-training to robot control, bridging the gap with large-scale whole-body human data—thoroughly aligned across observations and dynamics—proved essential. This approach offers a practical, powerful blueprint for scaling embodied intelligence models free from the constraints of robot hardware availability.

sections.heading: Appendix: State-Action Interfaces and Behind-the-Scenes Experimental Details
sections.summary: Provides mathematical definitions of the 44-dimensional state and 76-dimensional action spaces, rigorous dataset quality controls, and fitting methodologies for the scaling analysis.
sections.details:
The appendix details architectural and experimental choices omitted from the main text.

### State and Action Interface Definitions
For the G1 whole-body interface, actions are defined as 64-dimensional motion latents for the SONIC controller and 12-dimensional joint position commands for the BrainCo Revo2 hands (6 dimensions per hand, 76 dimensions total). Training incorporates real-time chunking (RTC), conditioning on up to an 8-step action prefix (history).

### Data Quality Verification and Scaling Protocols
To avoid evaluation leakage across the 500 hours of HumanVerse, splits are enforced strictly at the session level. For scaling law analysis, two subsets were curated: a "clean" set (top 25% annotation quality) and a "representative" set reflecting the broader distribution. Logarithmic fits quantify loss reduction per doubling of data scale.

takeaways: High-quality data for humanoid whole-body control can be collected at scale using just a neck-mounted GoPro and VR trackers, without needing physical robots.
Bridging embodiment gaps requires not just geometric retargeting, but offline dynamics-informed action alignment that accounts for controller tracking delays.
Inserting a whole-body mid-training stage that covers walking and squatting is far more crucial for real-world loco-manipulation success than hand-only pre-training.
Scaling human motion data yields monotonic improvements in real-robot task progress, confirming it as a promising roadmap for future embodied data collection.
limitations: In the SIMPLE benchmark evaluation, results rely on task-specific best checkpoints rather than a single unified checkpoint across all tasks, limiting strictly unified comparison.
Reliance on dynamics alignment and hand pose reconstruction pipelines risks error propagation in tasks with severe hand occlusion or high-impact physical contacts.
Real-world validation is restricted to a single platform, the Unitree G1, leaving cross-embodiment transferability to other commercial humanoids unverified.
